topic: User Research and Understanding User Needs
learningObjectives: Identify suitable user research methods for different design problems.
Distinguish qualitative and quantitative research data.
Create basic user insights from research findings.

activities.title: Research Method Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the most suitable research method for each scenario.

content.concept: Different research methods answer different questions. Interviews can explore motivations, surveys can collect measurable responses, observation reveals real behavior, usability testing evaluates interactions, and analytics reveals usage patterns.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Qualitative vs Quantitative
activities.instruction: Identify whether each research finding is qualitative or quantitative.

content.concept: Qualitative data describes experiences, behaviors, opinions, and motivations. Quantitative data represents measurable values such as counts, percentages, ratings, and completion rates.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: A participant's statement or explanation is qualitative evidence.
A description of what a participant actually does can provide qualitative behavioral evidence.
A percentage from a survey is quantitative data.
The percentage or number of users completing a task is quantitative data.
A repeated theme found across interviews is qualitative evidence.

activities.title: User Interview Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a focused user interview.

content.concept: A good interview begins with a clear research goal, builds rapport, asks open-ended questions, listens without leading the participant, and ends by organizing the findings.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

goal: 3. Introduce the session and build rapport

activities.title: Insight Extraction
activities.instruction: Choose the statement that represents the strongest UX insight.

content.concept: A useful UX insight goes beyond describing an observation. It connects behavior to a possible user need, motivation, or difficulty that can inform design decisions.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Observation: Three users abandoned checkout. Insight: Users may be uncertain about the final cost before confirming the purchase.
Observation: Three users abandoned checkout. Insight: Users do not like websites.
